did_you_know.text: Did you know? The heads of the Levite families approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the tribes at Shiloh to remind them of the command to give the Levites cities and pasturelands for their livestock.
Did you know? The descendants of Aaron, the priests, received thirteen cities by lot from the inheritances of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
Did you know? The remaining descendants of Kohath received ten cities from the inheritances of Ephraim, Dan, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
Did you know? The descendants of Gershon received thirteen cities from Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and half the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
Did you know? The descendants of Merari received twelve cities from the inheritances of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.

Did you know? Hebron, also called Kiriath-arba, was given to some of the descendants of Aaron, along with its pasturelands; however, the city's fields and surrounding land were given to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his inheritance.
Did you know? The total number of cities given to the descendants of Aaron the priests was thirteen, and each city had pasturelands around it.
Did you know? Among other cities, the descendants of Gershon received Golan in Bashan and Kedesh in Galilee, both of which were counted among the cities of refuge given to the Levites.
Did you know? In all, forty-eight cities within the inheritances of the Israelites were given to the Levites, and each city had pasturelands around it.
Did you know? At the end of the chapter, it says that the Lord gave Israel the whole land He had sworn to give their ancestors, and they took possession of it and settled there.
